t: This was the home of the Cavalry Club, a London gentlemen's club established in 1890. In 1975 it merged with the Guards' Club, and the Cavalry and Guards Club still exists today. Lieutenant Colonel William Leggatt died here in 1946. He was an army officer in the Royal Artillery, where he commanded artillery regiments during the North African campaign in the Second World War. He was also an amateur cricketer, who played eleven first-class matches between 1926 and 1933.
